facts.F162: Layer rule, decided per file (Confirmed, AFK recommended option in line with D-1): a move never splits a file. A file is Domain if and only if it is not a port file and every top-level type it declares has IL edges only to the kernel (Lighthouse.Backend.Models), the BCL and types of other Domain files. A port file declares an I-prefixed port interface; it stays in Application with every record and enum it declares, recorded as a declared fact on the membership map, not inferred. Every other file is Application. The Domain rule is one-way (R-R2): a Domain type reaches only the kernel, the BCL and other Domain types. The oracle also checks the reverse per non-port file: a kernel-only non-port file listed as Application fails. Whatever the IL gives as Domain is the answer (open question 4); SizingRefusal reaches Microsoft.Extensions.Logging, so it is Application; NeedBand is expected Domain, with any other kernel-only non-port file.
